title: Control mechanism of gas adsorption properties on energy release and Two-Phase flow during coal and gas outbursts
abstract: Coal–gas outbursts are governed not only by gas pressure but also by gas adsorption properties, yet how adsorption differences regulate the coupled evolution of energy release, coal fragmentation, and gas–coal two-phase flow transport remains unclear. To clarify this control mechanism, laboratory physical simulation experiments were conducted using a self-developed high-pressure outburst apparatus. CO 2 , N 2 , and He were selected to represent a strongly adsorptive gas, a weakly adsorptive gas, and a non-adsorptive reference gas, respectively. Under the same initial pressure of 0.74 MPa, CO 2 exhibited sustained pressure disturbances and a peak shock-wave overpressure of 25.49 kPa at 1.5 m from the outlet. The estimated total expansion energies of He, N 2 , and CO 2 were 13.2, 44.5, and 364.8 kJ/t, respectively, and desorption-induced expansion contributed 94.6% of the total CO 2 expansion energy. The attenuation coefficients of shock-wave overpressure were 0.104, 0.114, and 0.135 for CO 2 , N 2 , and He, respectively, indicating the slowest attenuation under strongly adsorptive conditions. The dust-bag mass fractions increased from 0.2% for He and 11.6% for N 2 to 22.7 % for CO 2 . A fractal-dimension inversion between N 2 and He further revealed that the final particle-size distribution was controlled by both initial fragmentation and aerodynamic sorting. A sequential mechanism of gas adsorption property–energy release mode–coal fragmentation–two-phase flow transport is proposed, providing a basis for gas-type-dependent outburst risk assessment.

title: A coupled THM ordinary state-based peridynamic model for dynamic rock fracture
abstract: The thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) coupled fracturing of rock under impact loading is a highly nonlinear process that poses challenges for classical numerical methods due to strong coupling and material discontinuities. To address this issue, a coupled dynamic THM ordinary state-based peridynamic (OSB-PD) framework is established by integrating nonlocal governing equations for mechanics, seepage, and heat transfer with a rate-thermal damage criterion. A radially symmetric correlated field shuffling (RSCFS) algorithm is proposed to generate symmetric correlated parameter fields for heterogeneous cylindrical specimens. An explicit time-integration solver incorporating a multi-time-step strategy and domain-decomposition parallelization is developed, together with a Delaunay-based energy mapping mass quantification (EMMP) module for energy-driven crack reconstruction. The model is calibrated and validated against multi-field coupled Hopkinson bar tests, and reproduces the measured responses with an average relative error below 6% and a coefficient of determination R 2 >0.95 under varied temperatures and pressures. Spatiotemporal THM coupling analysis reveals that thermo-mechanical interaction dominates near the crack tip, while hydro-mechanical coupling prevails in the bulk; fluid pressurization and thermal softening jointly govern fracture paths. This numerical tool is applicable to deep geological settings such as energy extraction, underground storage, and geohazard mitigation.

title: Kinetics-controlled low-temperature flotation separation of spodumene from albite using a mixed sodium oleate/betaine collector
abstract: Low-temperature flotation of spodumene is severely limited by sluggish interfacial kinetics rather than by insufficient collector adsorption, leading to poor separation from albite under cold conditions. In this study, a mixed collector system composed of sodium oleate (NaOL) and the environmentally friendly surfactant cocamidopropyl betaine (CAPB) was introduced to enhance flotation performance from a kinetic perspective. Micro-flotation results showed that the NaOL/CAPB system enabled effective separation of spodumene from albite at low temperatures, producing a significant recovery contrast of 69.78% at 10 °C while maintaining good selectivity at 5 °C, with a recovery difference of 62.95%. Flotation kinetics were described by a second-order model, and the NaOL/CAPB system significantly increased the flotation rate constant and kinetic selectivity index of spodumene compared with single collectors, indicating accelerated bubble-particle attachment kinetics. Interfacial analyses showed that CAPB reduced surface tension, improved froth properties, and promoted the formation of smaller and more stable bubbles, thereby facilitating bubble-particle attachment. Meanwhile, the selective adsorption of NaOL on spodumene provided the chemical basis for selectivity, while CAPB reorganized the interfacial adsorption layer and accelerated establishment of the three-phase contact line, thereby overcoming the kinetic limitations of spodumene flotation at low temperatures. This work demonstrates that regulating interfacial kinetics using a mixed NaOL/CAPB collector is an effective approach for enhancing spodumene flotation under cold conditions.

title: Time-dependent shear behavior and strength degradation of soft-hard interbedded rocks under loading perpendicular to bedding
abstract: Shear creep along potential failure surfaces in anti-dip interbedded slopes commonly occurs under cross-cut rather than bedding-parallel conditions, but this loading configuration has received limited attention. This study investigates the shear creep behavior and strength degradation of soft-hard interbedded rocks under cross-cut shear loading by combining laboratory tests, constitutive modelling, and three-dimensional numerical analysis. Rock-like specimens with hard-to-soft layer thickness ratios of 4:1 and 3:2 were subjected to shear creep loading perpendicular to bedding, followed by post-creep direct shear tests. The results show that both higher shear stress and a larger proportion of soft rock increase the steady-state creep rate and promote earlier transition to accelerated creep. The shear parameters (cohesion and internal friction angle) obtained after creep also show an overall reduction with creep history. Under relatively low shear stress, this degradation is limited, whereas under higher shear stress it becomes more pronounced with loading duration. Based on these observations, a coupled constitutive model was developed to describe the interaction among creep deformation, time-dependent degradation of shear strength parameters, and mechanical damage. The model reproduces the laboratory creep curves for both layer-thickness ratios, including the accelerated creep stage under high stress. It was then applied to a large cross-cut landslide at the Fushun West Open-Pit Mine, where the simulation reproduced the progressive development of the potential sliding surface and the late-stage acceleration of displacement. The study provides an experimental and modelling basis for evaluating the long-term stability of anti-dip soft-hard interbedded slopes under cross-cut shear conditions.

title: Modification of kaolinite/water interfacial hydration by OTAC and PAMT: Insights from AFM force spectroscopy and molecular dynamics
abstract: Understanding how hydrophobizing reagents modify the kaolinite/water interfacial environment is important for controlling kaolinite aggregation and solid-liquid separation in coal-slime systems. In this study, a combined experimental-simulation approach was employed to investigate the kaolinite-water-reagent system by integrating wettability, FTIR, XPS, zeta potential, particle-size analysis, and AFM force spectroscopy with molecular dynamics simulations. The addition of OTAC and PAMT significantly enhanced kaolinite hydrophobicity, as evidenced by increased contact angles and decreased surface free energy. Reagent adsorption also promoted particle aggregation, accompanied by a zeta-potential shift from −23 to −14 mV for OTAC and −4 mV for PAMT, and a reduction in AFM pull-off forces by 32 and 75 nN, respectively. Spectroscopic analyses confirmed organic reagent adsorption and indicated changes in the local chemical environment of hydroxylated and oxygen-containing surface groups, but they do not independently prove complete surface coverage or direct occupation of all hydration-active sites. OTAC mainly forms an alkyl-rich interfacial layer through the association of its quaternary ammonium headgroup with the kaolinite surface, whereas PAMT forms a polymeric adsorption layer involving multipoint attachment and bridging interactions. MD simulations further suggest reagent-induced restructuring of interfacial water, as reflected by changes in water-density profiles and weakened water-kaolinite interaction energies. Overall, the combined results support an inferred mechanism in which OTAC and PAMT adsorption modify hydration-active surface environments, reduce solid-water affinity, and promote kaolinite aggregation. PAMT exhibits stronger interfacial modification ability than OTAC because of its polymer-chain architecture and bridging capability. This AFM-MD coupled approach links reagent adsorption, interfacial water restructuring, and macroscopic aggregation responses, providing guidance for reagent design in coal-slime treatment.

title: Recent advances in sustainable oil sands tailings treatment: technologies and interfacial interaction mechanisms
abstract: The extraction and management of bitumen from Canadian oil sands pose significant environmental and operational challenges, chiefly due to the production of massive volumes of oil sands tailings. These tailings, particularly stable mature fine tailings (MFT), present formidable issues in terms of water entrapment, slow sedimentation, and ecological impacts. This comprehensive review examines the latest advancements in polymer flocculants and reviews the molecular interactions of tailing-water-polymer system. We begin with an overview of the oil sand tailings, their composition, and environmental and ecological impacts. Following this, we delve into the prevalent technologies for treating oil sands tailings, highlighting their strengths and limitations. Our focus then shifts to recent progress in tailings treatment strategies, with a special emphasis on the coagulants and polymer flocculants designed specifically for oil sands tailings. We also analyze the molecular interactions within the tailings–water–polymer system, offering insights into the mechanisms of action and the state-of-the-art techniques for studying colloidal interaction mechanisms in oil sands tailings treatment. The review culminates in a discussion of the challenges, limitations, and future perspectives of tailings management, underscoring the urgent need for innovative solutions in this field. Our findings indicate that despite substantial technological progress, most existing studies remain performance-oriented, lacking mechanistic quantification of interparticle forces and polymer-mediated interaction energy profiles. A critical knowledge gap persists in correlating molecular-scale interaction forces with macroscopic dewatering metrics such as initial settling rate, turbidity, and final solids content. Bridging this multiscale gap is essential for rational flocculant design.

title: Microseismic activity laws and warning method for radial chain rockbursts under the influence of moderately hard band in TBM tunnels
abstract: Radial chain rockbursts under the influence of moderately hard band (RCRs–mhb) pose significant safety risks in TBM tunnels. This study investigated the microseismic (MS) activity laws of RCRs–mhb and developed a total-to-single warning method. The RCRs-mhb exhibit a “chain” effect: a pre-fracture zone for a subsequent rockburst is formed due to the previous rockburst; the energy release and fracturing intensity in the subsequent rockburst area surge when the previous rockburst occurred; stress propagates deeper into surrounding rock after previous rockburst, triggering further fracturing. The maximum reduction in the ratio of cumulative MS apparent volume to cumulative MS apparent stress ( RAVAPPMR ) reflects the locked-in stress level of the moderately hard band, which positively correlates with total rockburst pit depth. The ratio of the decrease in static stress to the decrease in dynamic stress ( Y value) of RCRs-mhb single rockburst tends to increase. Considering the locked-in stress level, a warning method for RCRs-mhb total intensity was established based on RAVAPPMR . Considering the “chain” effect, a warning model for single rockburst of RCRs-mhb were established based on Gaussian Naive Bayes and Y value. The model was applied over a length of more than 2 km, with an overall warning accuracy exceeding 85%.

title: Investigation of intrinsic characteristics for Zhang-Zhu strength criterion based on three-dimensional stress space conversion
abstract: The Zhang-Zhu strength criterion shows intrinsic non-smoothness and non-convexity in the deviatoric plane. Although the modified Zhang-Zhu strength criteria resolve these drawbacks, their underlying mechanism remains insufficiently understood. This study converts the failure envelope of the Zhang-Zhu strength criterion from a polar coordinate system into an equivalent Cartesian coordinate system, revealing an approximately linear relationship between the square root of the second deviatoric stress invariant J 2 and the Lode angle θ σ in J 2 - θ σ plane. By simplifying the Zhang-Zhu strength criterion into a linear expression and performing stress space conversion, it is demonstrated that the approximately linear relationship corresponds to the non-convex failure envelope. Both theoretical comparison and validation against true triaxial test data confirm the accuracy of this approximately linear relationship, with the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 6.68% and misfitting rates S for twelve rocks remaining below 6.5%. True triaxial test data further demonstrates that rock failure follows the approximately linear relationship in J 2 - θ σ plane, establishing an intrinsic correlation between the true triaxial failure behavior and the non-convexity. Finally, parametric analysis indicates that the non-convexity intensifies with increasing rock parameter m i and unconfined compressive strength σ c but decreases with the first stress invariant I 1 .

title: Role of surrounding rock in coal and gas outburst induced by instability of deep gas-bearing coal–rock combination bodies
abstract: With increasing mining depth, the coupling effect between gas-bearing coal and surrounding rock intensifies, making the quantification of surrounding rock contributions one of the most challenging issues in coal and gas outburst (CGO) prevention and rock mechanics. This study employs a true triaxial outburst simulation system to compare CGO tests on gas-bearing coal-rock composites and pure coal samples under different vertical stresses. A mechanical and elastic energy (EE) model under surrounding rock disturbance was established to quantify their impact from an energy perspective. The results indicate that the roof significantly increases disaster intensity by 15.9%. Although the EE of the roof accounts for only 0.4%–2.7% of the total energy, elevated in-situ stress simultaneously enhances the EE of both the coal mass and the roof, creating a dual destructive effect of energy accumulation and transfer. This leads to a 14.3%–16.5% increase in the fragmentation work of the outburst coal mass, a 13.4%–18.3% increase in transport work, and an overall 11.6%–17.0% rise in disaster intensity. Coal-rock strength, impact tendency, excavation radius, and support all influence CGO. Under high in-situ stress, the surrounding rock not only triggers CGO but also releases EE. The amount of EE released may be close to the EE released by coal and the potential gas expansion energy.
